pageCache.pageTitle: St Charles Catholic Primary School |   Teaching British Values
pageCache.text:
Teaching British Values
Promoting British Values at St Charles
The Department for Education (DfE) has recently reinforced the need to create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty and mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.
At the heart of all we do at St Charles are the Gospel values of love, patience, truth, understanding and respect. British Values are seen as an integral part of this ethos and of the School’s Social, Moral, Spiritual and Cultural education for pupils. At St Charles British values are fostered and developed regularly in the following ways:
Democracy
Democracy is nurtured throughout the school. Pupils have the opportunity to have their voices heard through our School Council and Pupil Voice questionnaires and discussions. Members of the School Council are elected democratically by their peers every year. From September 2015, House Captains will be elected by pupils in Key Stage 2.
The Rule of Law
The importance of Laws, whether they be those that come from God, or those that govern the class, the school, or the country, are consistently reinforced throughout the school day and through school assemblies. Pupils are taught the value and reasons behind laws, how they govern and protect us, the responsibilities for individuals and the consequences that arise when laws are broken. Visits from authorities such as the Police, Fire Service, Magistrates, etc. help pupils to understand the Rule of Law and how it impacts on them and the wider society.
Individual Liberty
Within school, pupils are actively encouraged to make informed and sensible choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school, we provide our young people with an education that empowers them, whilst at the same time providing boundaries which allow them to make choices safely. Pupils are encouraged to know, understand and exercise their rights and personal freedoms and are advised how to exercise these safely, for example through our E-Safety and PSHE lessons.
Opportunities are given to pupils to demonstrate freedom of choice in lessons and at playtime.
We strongly believe that all pupils should have their voice listened to, whether at an academic level or a personal one. Adults are always available to listen to and support pupils.
Mutual Respect
The School motto of “Love God, Love Your Neighbour” encapsulates our desire and expectation that everyone in the school community should demonstrate respect. This is reflected in all curriculum policies as well as in classroom practice. The School’s Keys to Succeed and Golden Rules all reflect the expectation of mutual respect.
Assemblies regularly explore what respect is and how it is shown to those around us. Children are encouraged to help and support those less fortunate than themselves through our charity work and our work with the wider community.
Our school is very diverse. We cherish this diversity and celebrate it daily as well as at International Evening, Christmas concerts and other whole school events. Our curriculum reflects multi-culturalism, for example, we study texts, stories, music and art from a range of cultures. We are an inclusive school and do not tolerate any discrimination on the basis of race, gender or ability. In October we celebrate Black History Week with a range of activities, workshops and events. This serves to widen pupils knowledge and understanding and, consequently, to foster respect for everyone.
Tolerance of those of Different Faiths and Beliefs
This is achieved through enhancing pupils’ understanding of their place in a culturally diverse society and by giving them opportunities to experience such diversity. As well as studying the Catholic faith, we study other major faiths as part of our RE curriculum, including Judaism, Islam and Sikhism. Wherever possible, we explore the rituals and traditions of other faiths and belief groups including visiting their places of worship or inviting in representatives of those faiths.
Every year we hold an Anti-Bullying Week during which we discuss how to prevent prejudices and prejudice-based bullying as part of learning in PSHE. Our EAL department ensures that the languages and cultures of our school community are celebrated and actively displayed throughout the school. Language buddies help to support new pupils to the school and their parents who may not have English as a first language.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Charles Catholic Primary School |   Welcome from Our Executive Headteacher
pageCache.text:
Welcome from Our Executive Headteacher
Welcome to our Website.
Welcome to our website. At the heart of St Charles is a clear commitment to Catholic values where every child really does matter. The education that the pupils receive here has the Gospel values at its core and as one child explained to Ofsted during a recent inspection, “Our school motto, Love God, Love your neighbour”, really works here.
Good communication is essential in providing the best learning experience for our children. We have regular opportunities for you, as parents and carers, to meet with staff at the school (both informally and formally) to discuss your child’s progress and ways in which we can help them to move forward.
Our wide and varied curriculum is carefully planned to reflect current events. We believe the curriculum should be relevant to children’s life experiences; should inspire and engage them in learning, whilst enabling them to work collaboratively using their imaginations. The aim of our curriculum is for pupils to have requisite skills to be super successful, independent and motivated learners, in readiness for their next stage of education.
Our ultimate goal is to instill in our children a love of learning and a passion for life itself. We hope that this in turn will ensure that children leave St Charles Catholic Primary School as well rounded individuals who are fully equipped to deal with the opportunities and challenges that they will face in the future.
We invite you to come and visit our lovely school and witness first hand, all that we have to offer.
Please contact the school office by email (info@st-charles.rbkc.sch.uk) or call (0208 969 5566) to arrange a visit.
We look forward to meeting you and having the opportunity to work alongside you in years to come.

Remembering the Holy Souls during November
St Charles Book of the Holy Souls – November 2026
During November we remember all the members of our School community who have died and are on their way to Heaven. We list them in our special book and pray for their souls to help them with this journey.
We remember them every time we gather together as a community.
If you would like someone prayed for during November, please contact the Office for a form
On 11th November each year, we gather together at 11am for 2 minutes silence, followed by a Remembrance Liturgy.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Charles Catholic Primary School |   Service to others
pageCache.text:
On a Local Level
During the Autumn Term we celebrated our Harvest Festival with a special class assembly led by 2H. All children were asked to contribute non-perishable food items which were displayed as part of the assembly. The Chaplaincy then carried them around to Fr Peter Wilson at St Pius X Church . When the food arrives at the Church, the Parish Youth Group arrange the food into hampers which can be dispersed amongst needy families in the Parish at Christmas.
For information about the tradition of Harvest Festival click here.
The Chaplaincy deliver our Harvest Food to Fr Peter for distribution around the Parish.
The Christmas Raffle
Every Christmas the staff of the School donate items of food and drink that can be used as prizes for a Christmas raffle. All money raised is converted into Sainsbury’s vouchers and presented to Fr Peter during our School Carol service. Fr Peter gives the vouchers out to needy parishioners and families identified in the Parish to help them during the Christmas period.[/vc_column_text][/vc_column][/vc_row]
Performing for the Carmelite Sisters
At Christmas and Easter time the School Choir and Orchestra visit the Sisters of Carmel in the Convent next door. They sing carols and songs and play classical pieces of music to entertain the Congregation of Nuns.
The Sisters look forwards to these events ad the children enjoy performing for them.
At the end of the Autumn Term we always donate our Christmas Tree to the Sisters. They are very grateful and always look forward to receiving it.”]
On a National Level
Alan Morkill Care Home
Alan Morekill Care home is situated in St Mark’s Road, very close to the School.At Christmas and Easter we take children to visit the care home to sit and chat with the residents.The children will sing carol’s or songs from their recent assemblies and our musicians play pieces of music to entertain them. .The residence look forward to these visits and the children are regular invited back.
The Catholic Children’s Society
Each year we support the Catholic Children’s Society Lenten Appeal. We have an own clothes day for a £1 donation.The money is collected after Easter and presented to the Society during their Good Shepherd Mass at Westminster Cathedral.Pupils from Year 6 attend this and take part in the offertory.
We also support the CCS by attending their annual Christmas Carol Service, again at Westminster Cathedral. Children from Year 6 attend the service and present our donation during the arrival of the three kings.
For more information about the work of the CCS click here.
The British Legion Poppy Appeal
Every November, we support the British Legion Poppy Appeal.Every child and member of staff donate £1 for a poppy badge which is worn during our Remembrance Service on 11th November.
For more information about the work of the British Legion click here.
Macmillan Cancer Support Charity Coffee Morning
Each October, the staff and school raise money for Macmillan Cancer Support charity.All staff. parents and carers are invited to bake/buy cakes and biscuits to sell after School.This is so well supported that we usually need a second coffee morning to sell the remaining cakes.Any cakes unsold are sent next door to the Carmelite Monastery for the Sisters to enjoy.
More information about the work of the Macmillan Cancer Support Charity click here.
The NSPCC
Every two years, we invite a representative from the National Society for the Prevention of Cruelty to Children (NSPCC) to visit the School and to lead an assembly outlining the important work they do and where donated money is spent. The Chaplaincy then organise a sponsored event to raise funds. In the past these have included a sponsored read and a sponsored spell. In 2023 we raised £2,716.80
On an International Level
CAFOD
Last year we worked closely with CAFOD as part of our Jubilee Journey as Pilgrims of Hope.Della from CAFOD came to the School to begin this work. She led a whole School assembly and told us about Chirri and her family living in Africa, whose lives are affected by the effects of droughts.During this period of Lent, we have aksed our pupils to take home a colleciton box to collect spare change for the CAFOD appeal.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Charles Catholic Primary School |   Community and Church Links
pageCache.text:
Community and Church Links
Click on each title for more information about the local communities we serve.
THE CATHOLIC CHILDREN’S SOCIETY
The Catholic Children’s Society are situated on the south side of the St Charles Square. We have supported them over many years. We also attend their annual Christmas Liturgy and Good Shepherd mass at Westminster Cathedral. The School Chaplaincy have also helped in the Office and helped with administrative tasks.The CCS have also been incredibly generous to us by providing financial help to a number of our families through their crisis fund.
ST PIUS X CATHOLIC CHURCH
Fr Peter Wilson is our School Chaplain. He is the parish priest of St Pius X Catholic Church which is situated next door to us on the eastern side of St Charles Square. Fr Peter visits the School regularly and works closely with the RE Coordinator and the School Chaplaincy. We visit the Church regularly throughout the year for School Liturgies. Along with the parish, the School co-runs the Sacrament of Reconciliation and the Sacrament of the Eucharist programmes. Many of our pupils are altar servers. We also donate our Harvest Festival contributions to the parish soup kitchen and to needy families of the parish each Autumn. We also hold a Christmas raffle to raise money for parish families at Christmas.
The Sisters of Carmel are our neighbours. The choir and orchestra visit them every Christmas and Easter to perform for them. We sing carols and play beautiful pieces of music for them as an orchestra as well as solo pieces. This is our way of saying thank you to them for remembering our School community in their prayers each day.
Alan Morkill Nursing Home
Alan Morkill Nursing home is situated in St Mark’s Road, very close to our School. The children visit the Home at Christmas and Easter to talk to the residents and to sing carols and songs from their assemblies. Many of our musicians play pieces of music they have learned much to the pleasure of the staff and residents.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Charles Catholic Primary School |   Ethos and Values
pageCache.text:
Ethos and Values
The whole School community were involved in selected the above values. We believe they reflect Our School very well.
At St. Charles Catholic Primary School we believe that each child should learn in an atmosphere surrounded by love.
We aim to promote a learning atmosphere where positive values in behaviour and attitudes are created and where every child is given the opportunity to develop his/her true potential academically, morally and spiritually.The children in our care will be taught to value each other and the world around them. In dealing with others they will show forgiveness and patience, ready to comfort those in need. They will be taught to appreciate the aesthetic value of the world we inhabit. Opportunities to do this will be sought across the subject range both in the academic and the more creative aspects of the curriculum.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Charles Catholic Primary School |   Meet the Chaplaincy Team
pageCache.text:
Meet The Chaplaincy Team
Grace
I am very grateful for the chance to be in the Chaplaincy so I can talk about Jesus with other children in the School and share my faith with them. I want to show how we can look after God’s creation by recycling and not wasting food.
Anna
I really enjoy helping others, and I think being in the Chaplaincy would be a great way to do that. I want to support children with their prayers and make collective worship a special time for everyone. I’m also looking forward to talking about God with others, sharing my faith, and helping theirs—and mine—grow stronger. I hope to be someone they can come to for support and encouragement.
Elouise
I love God and I want to serve him in the Chaplaincy. I want to help other children with their prayers and help them with their collective Worship. I am looking forward to talking with other people about God.
Haidy
I love God and I want to help others understand what I believe. I would like to be part of the Chaplaincy so I can help and be a good friend. I want to help people feel welcome and happy. I like learning about different beliefs and sharing mine too.
Ibe
I really love God and want to help others learn about Him. Being part of the Chaplaincy would let me serve and praise God every day, encourage others to do the same, and support them in worship. I’d enjoy leading prayers, talking about faith, and being someone others can look up to.
Gabby
I will let the children in school know about everything we have discussed and let them know how to improve the way they serve God and how to strengthen their faith.
Salvador
I want to be part of the Chaplaincy because I want to help people feel less alone and be a good role model to others. Chaplaincy is important to me because I want to help people and children learn their prayers and grow in their faith. Being part of the Chaplaincy makes me feel that I am doing the work God wants me to do by spreading His message of love and kindness. I believe our prayer time is a respectful moment to spend with God and an opportunity for everyone to reflect, pray and feel closer to Him.
Ayonie
I would like to be part of the Chaplaincy so that I can share the experience with my friends and work together as a team to help others. I would be very proud to wear my Chaplaincy badge and represent our school. Being part of the Chaplaincy would help me to grow closer to God and strengthen my own faith. I would also like to help other children around the school express and develop their relationship with God, whether through prayer, Mass or by simply being there to listen and support them. I think being a member of the Chaplaincy is a special responsibility because I can be a positive role model and help make our school a caring and faith-filled community.
Albie
I enjoy putting the religious things I learn in school into practice and developing my faith. I really enjoy representing our school at church, taking part in Mass, doing readings and arriving early to help prepare everything. I would like to be part of the Chaplaincy so that I can help younger children with their prayers and help them understand the Gospel. I feel proud to represent our school and share my faith with others.
Leonardo
I want to be part of the Chaplaincy because I want to grow closer to God and strengthen my faith. I would like to help younger children learn their prayers and support them in developing their relationship with God. I would also be proud to represent our school at Mass and be a good role model for other pupils.
